svg.text: Shakti E-class → ALPANA: pipeline dataflow, 3-stage to 4-stage
Stage boxes are BSV modules (stage0..stage3); every ||| is a pipeline FIFO (mkLFIFOF). Orange marks the 80 MHz timing-fix registers.
A. Stock Shakti E-class: 3 stages, RV32IMAC, 50 MHz
Critical path: PC mux → fetch → align/decompress → decode → RF read all in one cycle; branch redirect drives the PC combinationally. Fmax ≈ 50 MHz.
B. ALPANA: 4 stages + SP FPU, RV32IMAFC, 80 MHz
trap / flush → PC + epochs (same-cycle epoch fix)
C. What the extra stage does to one taken branch
redirect resolved in EX, PC updated same cycle
= the ~5 % CPI cost; paid back by 50 → 80 MHz (1.6×)
Net: CPI 9.15 → 9.69 (+5.9 %) · clock 50 → 80 MHz (+60 %) · DMIPS 5.72 → 8.64 (1.51×) · CoreMark 21.1 → 32.2 (1.53×) · FP matmul 28× (FPU vs soft-float)
Both cores remain fetch-bound (~6 cycles per 32-bit fetch over AXI, no I-cache), which is why pipeline depth moves CPI only a few percent.
